examples.name: Default
examples.summary: Headings, paragraphs, links, inline code, both list kinds, a blockquote and a section rule: the plain semantic HTML a Markdown source renders to through `DocMarkdown`, none of it carrying a class. `DocProse` styles it the way it styles a documentation page.

examples.name: ChromeBoundary
examples.summary: `DocProse` styles descendants, so without a guard it would restyle the internals of every documentation component sitting in the prose — a callout body, a code block’s lines, an accordion trigger’s heading. Every prose rule carries `:not([data-doc-chrome],[data-doc-chrome]_*)`, so a subtree marked `data-doc-chrome` is left alone while the prose around it is not.
